Only bzip2recover is affected; that utility is absent. libbz2 decompression is not the affected component.
Application filenames never supply a libc fopen mode. Python validates modes; Node uses numeric open flags and Java uses fixed modes. Native codecs use fixed modes, not request-supplied ccs strings.
No application/dependency import of strfmon or strfmon_l; the service does not offer locale monetary formatting.
No external tdelete caller; loader/unwind bookkeeping handles the fixed application libraries, not an attacker-supplied million-node search tree.
The affected DNS diagnostic formatting APIs are not the ordinary getaddrinfo resolver and have no application imports.
No use of the affected DNS diagnostic formatter, including through native libraries.
No shell or native wordexp caller. Python subprocess passes fixed argument arrays.
No wordexp/tilde expansion of untrusted values; shell payload removed.
The affected SHIFT_JISX0213 gconv module is physically removed and its removal verified.
The affected EUC-JISX0213 gconv module is physically removed and its removal verified.

Empty LOCALDOMAIN selects the bounded empty search list and skips resolv.conf search/domain/hostname fallback. Python startup enforces it for itself and subprocesses; CI initializes and reloads against a long search list.
The attack requires AT_SECURE privileged execution. No set-ID files or file capabilities remain; the service uses an unprivileged UID with no-new-privileges.
The nscd daemon is absent; the ordinary stub resolver is a different component.
The affected secure loader path requires privilege-changing execution, which the runtime image and process policy exclude.

Only exact-hash FFmpeg image-sequence and Kerberos configuration callers may remain. FFmpeg video I/O is disabled and the app accepts bounded in-memory JPEG/JP2 only. Registry connections force TLS/SCRAM with GSS disabled; GSS also uses a fixed configuration glob, not request-supplied patterns. Other native glob imports block.

PyTorch test executables are removed. Only the exact-hash Kerberos local-name mapping caller may remain; registry connections require SCRAM and disable GSS encryption, so requests cannot reach Kerberos mapping rules. Python/Java regular expressions use different engines. Any other regcomp/regexec import blocks.

Upstream classifies this stack-guard claim as a non-security bug/no real threat. It assumes an independently exploitable stack overflow. This determination does not assert that memory-safety bugs are impossible.
ldd is physically removed. The application does not inspect or execute user-supplied ELF files.
Upstream disputes this ASLR claim; predictable layout after allocation is not an independently demonstrated disclosure in these services.
Upstream disputes treating pthread_t address information, available to code already executing in the process, as an independent vulnerability.

SQLite Session changeset APIs are not exposed by CPython sqlite3 or imported by the application. Extension loading is disabled. ENABLE_SESSION may be compiled in; the claim is not code absence.
The service uses fixed SQL and bound parameters, not Session changeset merge/apply APIs. Dynamic extension loading is disabled.

SQLite upstream states this reads bytes from the supplied database file, not unrelated process memory. Recovery uses fixed queries and verified backup bindings; corrupt database content remains untrusted. Not justified by assuming all backup files are trustworthy.
Debian does not build the optional zipfile extension; the live module list excludes it and SQL extension loading is unauthorized.

No external callers of crc32_combine64/crc32_combine_gen64 accept a negative length. Python 3.12 does not expose these entry points.
No caller of gzprintf/gzvprintf exists; ordinary bounded inflate/deflate operations do not reach this nonblocking gzwrite-then-format sequence.
PSF fixes the Linux symlink-safe cleanup path in 3.12.15; 3.12.16 includes the fix. CI requires rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks and tests cleanup without following symlinks.
The unused imaplib module and bytecode are removed; no IMAP client is exposed.
The unused poplib module and bytecode are removed; no POP client is exposed.
Project decoding uses only the standard alphabet with validate=True, never altchars or urlsafe_b64decode. Identity verification does not use dependency decoders as an authorization boundary.
Every application Base64 decode uses validate=True, the PSF mitigation. Trailing padded groups/junk are rejected in runtime probes.
No request-supplied pkgutil.get_data path; upstream disputes this documentation/API-contract report. Locked dependency resource loads use trusted package resources.
SimpleCookie parses HTTP headers; no Morsel.js_output or generated cookie JavaScript is used.
No XML_ParserReset exposed in the Python service. pyexpat parsers are single-document; ordinary ElementTree creates/frees parsers. Public payloads are JSON; SAML is parsed by Java, not Expat.

No attacker-supplied XML reaches Expat: public handlers accept bounded JSON, and the three fixed AWS runtime clients use JSON protocols. S3/STS operator tooling is outside these images. Native image codecs and fixed local models are separate parsers.
No attacker-supplied XML reaches Expat; the greater-than-2^30-attribute trigger also exceeds all service request limits. Java SAML does not use this parser.
